deep.reconstruction:
Context: Gauss's magnetometer observations (1830s; previous page dated 'Mai 1'). A loaded magnetic needle is used to find its moment of inertia by placing weights (200 g in two pieces) at different distances from the axis (Gauss's Intensitas method). Transit times through the scale mark are recorded and reduced to the oscillation period.

(A) Correction for finite amplitude ('Correction jedes Zeitmoments wegen der nicht unendlich kleinen Schwingung'). Gauss writes the correction to each observed passage time as C = p^2*T/21887500, with log10(21887500) = 7.34020. Here T is the duration of one swing (a half-period) and p is the arc of swing in scale divisions. The denominator is proportional to the logarithmic decrement: it becomes 21887500*h/0.00126 if a decrement h replaces 0.00126.

My reconstruction of why the correction has this form:
- A swing of angular amplitude alpha lasts T0*(1 + alpha^2/16).
- With damping, alpha_k = alpha_n*e^(-lambda*k).
- Define S_n = sum over k>=0 of T*alpha_{n+k}^2/16 = T*alpha_n^2/(16*(1 - e^(-2*lambda))), which is approximately T*alpha_n^2/(32*lambda).
- Then t_{n+1} - t_n = T0 + S_n - S_{n+1}. Hence the corrected times t_n + S_n form an exact arithmetic progression with the period for infinitely small swings, T0.
- Since alpha is proportional to p, S_n = p^2*T/N with N proportional to lambda. This explains both the positive correction and the scaling note N(h) = 21887500*h/0.00126.
- If alpha = p/(4R) (full arc p, mirror doubling the angle, R = mirror-scale distance in scale divisions) and h is a Briggsian decrement (lambda = h*ln 10), then N = 512*ln(10)*h*R^2. This gives R of about 3840 divisions. The geometric interpretation is my assumption.
- The previous page confirms how the formula is used. The arcs 263.9, about 201 and 155.9 give the listed corrections +0.056, +0.034 and +0.020. The corrected times give the periods 17.6294, 17.6196, 17.6101 and 17.6073.

(B) Continuation of the previous series (swing time about 17.63 s).
- For swings 397-401 the reduced time is t_n - n*17.63: 23h42'5.72 - 397*17.63 s = 21h45'26.61, then 26.56, 26.53, 26.50, 26.51.
- Their mean, 21h45'26.542, is exactly the '399 26.542' entry used on the previous page.

(C) New series: same load, weights at distance 177.45; trial swing time 20.27 s.
- Reduced times t_n - 20.27*n: swings 1, 2, 5, 6 give 15'46.33, .41, .60, .65. Swings 127, 128, 133, 134 give 48.67, .64, .60, .55. Swings 493, 494, 499, 500 give 47.86, .77, .73, .71. Swings 550-552 give 47.30, .28, .21.
- Group means: at 3.5, 46.4975 (written 46.50); at 130.5, 48.615; at 496.5, 47.7675; at 551, 47.2633.
- Scale readings at swings 130/131, 496/497 and 554/555: the second column (304.9, 304.1; 92.6, 92.2; 77.1, 77.3) is the decaying arc p.
- Swing times from differences of the group means: 20.27 + 2.115/127 = 20.2867; 20.27 - 0.848/366 = 20.2677; 20.27 - 0.504/54.5 = 20.2608.
- These match exactly without the amplitude corrections. So on this page the correction of (A) has not yet been applied to the 177.45 series; it would be about 0.086 s at p = 305, 0.008 at p = 92 and 0.0055 at p = 77.
- The decrease of T along the series reflects the amplitude effect plus a residual drift, which is also seen after correction on the previous page.
errors: Swing 493: the time read as 3h2'20.75 gives a reduced time of 15'47.64, not the 47.86 written. 47.86 requires 3h2'20.97, which also fits the interval to swing 494 (20.18 instead of 20.40). Either the reading is wrong ('20.95/20.97' read as 20.75) or the time was miswritten; the 47.86 is used in the mean 47.767.
The swing times 20.2867, 20.2677 and 20.2608 are computed from uncorrected means. They are therefore not yet reduced to infinitely small arcs; this is not an error if the correction was to follow.

The observed decrement in the 177.45 series is about 0.0014 (Briggs), for example log10(304.9/92.6)/366 = 0.00141. This is larger than 0.00126, which is presumably why Gauss notes how the denominator scales with h.

results.what: Cumulative finite-amplitude correction for damped oscillation: add p^2*T/N to each passage time, with N proportional to the logarithmic decrement, so that the corrected times form an arithmetic progression with the infinitesimal-arc period
results.modern_name: Reduction of oscillation period to infinitesimal amplitude (alpha^2/16 term) summed over a geometrically decaying amplitude
results.usually_credited_to: alpha^2/16 correction: Euler/D. Bernoulli (18th c.); damped-magnetometer reductions: Gauss and Weber, Resultate des magnetischen Vereins (1830s)

results.what: Reduction of transit times by subtracting n*T_trial and averaging groups to obtain the swing time
results.modern_name: Gauss's method of observing oscillation times (reduced transit times / linear fit of passages)

results.what: Oscillation series with added weights at different distances to determine the moment of inertia
results.modern_name: Gauss's absolute method for magnetic intensity (moment of inertia by added masses)

deep.surprise_reason: Laboratory notebook data reduction in Gauss's own well-documented magnetometer method. The damping-dependent cumulative amplitude correction is a neat but known part of his and Weber's published practice.
